In general terms: a board-approved IT strategy and IT risk framework, controlled IT operations and projects, protection of confidential information, IT resilience and continuity, IT assurance and notice of material IT incidents. It also expects IT-related training for people with access to IT systems.
- **Joint Standard 2 of 2024 (PA and FSCA):** the cyber layer: governance, controls, awareness training, testing, incident response and notice of material cyber incidents.
- **POPIA (Information Regulator):** the privacy layer: lawful processing, security safeguards and breach notification for personal information.

One strong control often serves several rules at once, but each rule must be evidenced on its own terms.

cards.title: The Joint Standard 2 review clock
cards.caption: Minimum cycles stated in Joint Standard 2 of 2024. The standard expects more frequent action where risk requires it.

items.label: Cyber strategy review
items.detail: Reviewed regularly and at least yearly for threats, resources, gaps and lessons.

items.label: Independent framework review
items.detail: Adequacy and effectiveness checked at least yearly by audit or a control function.

items.label: User refresher training
items.detail: Every user refreshed at least yearly, with new content added regularly.

items.label: Internet-facing pen tests
items.detail: At every major change, and at least yearly if there is none.

items.label: Asset inventory review
items.detail: Updated when things change and reviewed at least every two years.

cards.title: Which instrument mainly says it?
cards.prompt: Sort each requirement into the instrument that mainly carries it.

items.text: Assess policies against the Basel operational resilience principles
Align resilience with critical functions in recovery and resolution plans
Run scenario-based simulation exercises including an adversarial attack and defence
Report security control deficiencies that cannot be fixed in time to the governing body
Register the information officer with the Regulator
Notify affected people of a personal information compromise
Train the governing body on technology and cyber risk
Apply the principles on a consolidated basis across the group

cards.title: When the systems went dark at the ports

lines.text: Everyone talks about banks, but my favourite resilience lesson is from Transnet in 2021. Their port systems went down after a security breach.
I remember the queues of trucks. What saved them?
Manual processes. Bulk and automotive cargo switched to manual straight away, and they brought the container system back in about a week. They also set up a daily line to their big customers.
That's operational resilience in a sentence: know your critical operations, have a workaround, talk to your customers, recover in a planned order.

cards.title: Real case: Transnet's port systems, July 2021
cards.body:
On the morning of 22 July 2021 Transnet, the state-owned port and rail operator, suffered an IT security breach that disrupted its port systems. Government's statement on gov.za a week later reported:

- **Manual fallback:** bulk, break-bulk and automotive operations that used the general cargo system switched to manual processes immediately, limiting disruption. Rail kept running to plan.
- **Prioritised recovery:** the main container terminal operating system was fully restored, with remaining systems brought back in stages to reduce further risk.
- **Customer engagement:** the minister and Transnet set up a platform for regular meetings with affected customers' senior representatives.
- **Data:** the preliminary assessment indicated that Transnet and customer data had not been compromised, with investigations under way.

**Lessons for a bank under Directive 4 and Joint Standard 2:** map critical operations and their dependencies, pre-plan manual workarounds, restore in a planned order, and communicate with customers throughout.

*Source: Ministry of Public Enterprises statement on gov.za, 29 July 2021.*

cards.title: Skipping the simulation
cards.situation: The board's IT and risk committee is asked to approve this year's cyber testing plan. To save money, the COO proposes dropping the planned scenario-based simulation exercise with an attack-and-defence component, arguing that 'we just had a real incident in Durban, so we've been tested'.

choices.text: Approve the COO's proposal; a real incident is the best test.
choices.outcome: A real incident gives lessons, but Joint Standard 2 requires regular scenario-based simulation exercises, including an adversarial attack and defence exercise, designed from relevant threat intelligence. One incident does not replace that.

choices.text: Keep the exercise, design it from current threat intelligence and the Durban lessons, and track any findings through remediation with timelines reported to the committee.
choices.outcome: Best answer. It meets the standard's simulation requirement, uses the real incident to sharpen the scenario, and feeds results into the remediation process the board must oversee.

choices.text: Replace it with an extra penetration test of the website.
choices.outcome: Penetration testing is also required, but it checks specific systems. It does not test response, recovery and communication plans the way a simulation does.

choices.text: Postpone the decision until after the PA review.
choices.outcome: Delay leaves a known gap in front of the supervisor and does not show the board exercising oversight of cyber testing.

cards.title: Getting ready for the PA review
cards.prompt: Put Marula's readiness steps in a sensible order.
steps: Confirm the critical operations, their dependencies and tolerances for disruption
Check the cyber strategy, framework and policies are approved and within their review dates
Gather training evidence: user refreshers, new-content sessions, board training and the programme review
Test: penetration tests, simulation exercise and backup restoration
Track findings in the remediation process with severity and timelines
Report the overall position and open gaps to the board committee

cards.title: Who owns what at Marula Bank
cards.prompt: Match each role to its main responsibility in this quest.

pairs.right: Ultimately responsible; approves cyber strategy and framework; is trained on cyber risk
Runs the cyber framework with authority, resources and access to the board
Encourages and ensures POPIA compliance and works with the Information Regulator
Completes training, follows access and data rules, reports lures and incidents promptly
Builds security and breach-notice terms into contracts and checks providers' controls
Independently reviews the cyber framework at least yearly

cards.title: Prioritising what to protect and recover first
cards.caption: Joint Standard 2 asks banks to classify processes and assets by criticality and sensitivity and to use that to prioritise protection, detection, response and recovery.

items.label: Protect and rehearse
items.detail: High criticality, high sensitivity: core banking, payments, customer data stores.

items.label: Recover fast
items.detail: High criticality, lower sensitivity: ATM availability, branch teller and queue systems.

items.label: Lock down
items.detail: Lower criticality, high sensitivity: HR files, archived loan scans.

items.label: Standard care
items.detail: Lower criticality, lower sensitivity: intranet news, cafeteria menus.

cards.question: Under Joint Standard 2, what must happen when testing finds security control deficiencies that cannot be fixed in a timely way?
options: They must be escalated and reported to the governing body
They can be closed if the vendor disagrees
They must be reported only to the Information Regulator
They must be hidden until the next audit
cards.explanation: Paragraph 7.7.1 requires the bank to escalate and report to the governing body any testing results that identify deficiencies that cannot be remediated in time, and to follow a remediation plan with timelines.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: Directive 4 of 2023 made the Basel operational resilience principles binding on banks, with compliance due by 31 December 2024.
The seven categories run from governance to resilient ICT including cyber security; the PA can require extra capital if resilience is inadequate.
Joint Standard 2's minimum cycles: yearly strategy review, independent framework review, refreshers and internet-facing pen tests; asset inventory every two years.
Simulation exercises must include an adversarial attack and defence; unresolved deficiencies go to the board.
Readiness means evidence: approvals, training records, test results, remediation tracking and board reporting.

cards.prompt: If your part of the bank lost its main system for a week, what would your manual workaround be, who depends on you, and who would you need to keep informed?

quiz.question: Which international document does Directive 4 of 2023 require South African banks to implement?
options: The FATF Recommendations
ISO 27001 certification
The EU's General Data Protection Regulation
The Basel Committee's principles for operational resilience (March 2021)
quiz.explanation: Directive 4 of 2023 directs banks to assess and implement the principles in the BCBS paper on operational resilience published in March 2021.

quiz.question: Which directive did Directive 4 of 2023 replace?
options: Directive 1 of 2026
Directive 10 of 2021
Directive 2 of 2019
Joint Standard 1 of 2023
quiz.explanation: Directive 4 of 2023 states that it replaces Directive 10 of 2021 and extends the compliance date.

quiz.question: If the PA finds a bank's operational resilience policies inadequate, what may it require under the Banks Act regulations as described in Directive 4?
options: Immediate closure of all branches
Additional capital, or alignment of policies with the bank's risk exposure
A criminal prosecution of the board
A transfer of the licence to the FSCA
quiz.explanation: The directive notes that regulation 38(4) lets the PA require extra capital or require the bank to align its resilience policies with its risk exposure.

quiz.question: Under Joint Standard 2, when must penetration testing be done on systems directly accessible from the internet?
options: Whenever they undergo major changes, and at least yearly if there are none
Only once, when the system is first launched
Every five years
Only after a material incident
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.7.3 requires penetration testing of internet-facing systems whenever they undergo major changes or updates, and at least annually if no major changes are made.

quiz.question: What must Joint Standard 2's scenario-based simulation exercises include?
options: A fire drill only
An adversarial attack and defence exercise
A review of the marketing budget
A customer satisfaction survey
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.7.4 requires regular scenario-based simulation exercises that include, but are not limited to, an adversarial attack and defence simulation, designed from relevant threat intelligence.

quiz.question: Which of the seven Basel resilience categories most directly covers a bank's reliance on its cloud provider?
options: Third-party dependency management
Governance
Information quality
Data subject participation
quiz.explanation: Third-party dependency management covers risks from service providers that critical operations depend on. Information quality and data subject participation are POPIA conditions.

quiz.question: In the 2021 Transnet case reported on gov.za, what limited disruption for bulk and automotive cargo?
options: An immediate switch to manual processes
Paying the attackers
Closing the ports for a month
Moving cargo to another country's ports
quiz.explanation: Government's statement said bulk, break-bulk and automotive operations switched immediately to manual processes, which resulted in minimal disruption.

quiz.question: Under Joint Standard 2, what must the bank do with issues found in cybersecurity testing?
options: Delete them once the test report is filed
Send them to customers for comment
Fix them only if the vendor agrees
Track them in a remediation process with severity, priority and timeframes
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7.7.6 requires a comprehensive remediation process including severity classification, risk-based prioritisation, timeframes by severity and tracking of all issues.

quiz.question: Directive 4 of 2023 asks banks to harmonise their resilience approach with which other planning?
options: The critical functions and shared services in recovery and resolution plans
The bank's staff social calendar
Its marketing campaign plans
The Information Regulator's annual plan
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2.1.5 asks banks to consider whether their resilience approach is harmonised with the actions, mappings and critical functions in their recovery and resolution plans.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes how Joint Standard 1 of 2023 relates to Joint Standard 2 of 2024?
options: Joint Standard 1 sets IT governance and risk rules; Joint Standard 2 adds specific cyber requirements
Joint Standard 1 applies only to insurers
Joint Standard 2 repealed Joint Standard 1
They are voluntary industry guidelines
quiz.explanation: Joint Standard 1 covers IT governance and risk management in general; Joint Standard 2 sets cybersecurity and cyber resilience requirements. Both are binding standards that apply side by side.

references.title: Joint Standard 2 of 2024: Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Requirements for Financial Institutions (published with Joint Communication 2 of 2024)
references.provision: Paragraphs 3-9, especially 7.2.7 (awareness and training), 7.5 (incident response) and 9.1 (notification)
references.note: Applies to banks, branches, controlling companies and mutual banks. Requires a board-approved cyber strategy and framework, controls, an awareness programme for all users with at least yearly refreshers and board training, testing, incident response and notice of material incidents.

references.title: Joint Notice 2 of 2026: Determination of the Notification Template for Material IT and Cyber Incidents
references.note: Sets the template banks file on the PA's Umoja portal when an IT or cyber incident is classified as material, under JS1 para 15.1 and JS2 para 9.1; in force from 1 September 2026.

references.title: Annexure A: Reporting of Material IT and/or Cyber Incident Template
references.note: Immediate notification within 24 hours of classifying an incident as material; an impact update within 14 calendar days of notification; a full report with the final investigation report on timelines agreed with the authority.

references.title: FSCA-PA Joint Communication 5 of 2026: Determination of the notification template for material IT and cyber incidents
references.note: Publishes the determination, template and consultation report; confirms Joint Standard 1 took effect on 15 November 2024 and Joint Standard 2 on 1 June 2025, and that the determination applies from 1 September 2026.

references.title: Joint Standard 1 of 2023: IT Governance and Risk Management Requirements for Financial Institutions (published with Joint Communication 4 of 2023)
references.note: Board responsibility, an approved IT strategy and IT risk framework reviewed at least yearly, IT resilience and continuity, and notice of material IT incidents; also expects IT-related training for people with access to IT systems.

references.title: Directive 4 of 2023 (D4/2023): Directive on operational resilience
references.note: Issued under Banks Act s 6(6); replaces Directive 10 of 2021. Banks must assess themselves against the BCBS operational resilience principles in seven categories, apply them on a consolidated basis and comply by 31 December 2024.

references.title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013
references.issuer: Parliament (Department of Justice and Constitutional Development)
references.note: Eight conditions for lawful processing; security safeguards (s 19); operators (ss 20-21); notification of compromises to the Regulator and data subjects as soon as reasonably possible (s 22); information officer duties; civil, criminal and administrative consequences.

references.title: Regulations relating to the Protection of Personal Information, 2018 (GN R.1383, Government Gazette 42110)
references.note: As originally made, the information officer had to make sure internal awareness sessions are held on POPIA; the regulations were amended in April 2025 and the amended text could not be opened, so the quest does not rely on this duty.

references.title: The Department of Justice's IT system attacked by ransomware (media statement)
references.issuer: Department of Justice and Constitutional Development (gov.za)
references.note: Real case: ransomware on 6 September 2021 encrypted the department's systems; it activated its business continuity plan and noted that ransomware often spreads through phishing emails and drive-by downloads.

references.title: Update on progress in restoring justice services following ransomware attack (media statement)
references.issuer: Department of Justice and Constitutional Development (gov.za)
references.note: Real case: the malware was contained, services were restored in stages, a POPIA notice was issued to data subjects on the department's website, and security and access control were strengthened.

references.title: Minister Pravin Gordhan commends Transnet for restoring full ports operations (media statement)
references.note: Real case: after an IT security breach on 22 July 2021, Transnet switched bulk operations to manual, restored its container terminal system in stages and engaged customers daily.

references.title: Fraud and Scams
references.note: The SARB warns that syndicates abuse its logo and employee names in advance-fee scams, and that it does not hold accounts or cross-border funds for members of the public.

bank.question: A foreign bank operates a branch in Johannesburg. Its head office argues that the group's global cyber policy is enough and that Joint Standard 2 does not reach a branch. Which view is correct?
options: The branch is exempt because the parent is supervised abroad
The branch is a financial institution under the standard and must meet it
Only the FSCA's conduct standards apply to the branch
The branch must comply only once it has 500 staff
bank.explanation: The definition of financial institution in Joint Standard 2 includes a branch of a foreign institution as defined in the Banks Act. A global policy can help, but the branch must meet the standard.

bank.question: During the PA's review, the bank shows that its cyber framework was last independently reviewed 20 months ago. What is the problem?
options: Nothing, because a review every two years is allowed
The framework must be reviewed monthly by the board
Only the strategy needs review; the framework is fixed
The framework must be reviewed at least annually through an independent review
bank.explanation: Joint Standard 2 requires the cybersecurity framework to be reviewed regularly but at least annually for adequacy and effectiveness through an independent review. Two years applies to the asset inventory.

bank.question: Which of these best describes what 'independent review' means in Joint Standard 2?
options: A review by the team that designed the control
A review by any staff member outside IT
A review by the Information Regulator
A review by internal or external audit or an independent control function
bank.explanation: The standard defines an independent review as one carried out by an internal or external audit function or an independent control function.

bank.question: Marula Bank's learning team proposes moving the cyber awareness refresher to every 18 months to save time, while sending monthly tips. Is this compliant?
options: No: refresher training must happen at least yearly, whatever tips are added
Yes, because monthly tips replace the formal refresher
Yes, if the board approves the longer cycle
No, because refresher training must happen every quarter
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.2.7 requires user refresher training at least annually and regular new content. Tips can support the programme but do not stretch the yearly minimum.

bank.question: A board member says the board can hand the whole cyber topic to its risk committee and stop worrying about it. What does Joint Standard 2 allow?
options: Transferring all responsibility to the committee
Delegating primary oversight work to a committee while the board stays ultimately responsible
Transferring responsibility to the CISO by resolution
Removing cyber from the board agenda once a committee exists
bank.explanation: The governing body may delegate primary oversight activities to an existing or new committee, but it remains ultimately responsible for compliance and for cyber risk oversight.

bank.question: Which pair of documents must the governing body approve under Joint Standard 2?
options: The firewall rule set and the patch schedule
The cybersecurity strategy and the cybersecurity framework
Each staff member's training record
Every penetration test report
bank.explanation: The strategy must be approved by the governing body and aligned with business strategy, and the framework must also be approved by the governing body.

bank.question: A bank's information asset inventory records each asset's location, but not who owns it or who manages it. Which requirement is not met?
options: The inventory must include location, ownership and management roles
The inventory must be published on the bank's website
The inventory must list only paper records
The inventory must be approved by the FSCA
bank.explanation: Joint Standard 2 requires an inventory of information assets that includes location, ownership and the roles and responsibilities for managing them, reviewed at least every two years.

bank.question: The cyber function at a bank reports to the head of IT operations, who decides its budget and whose systems it audits. What governance concern does Joint Standard 2 raise?
options: None, because reporting lines are a matter for HR
The function must report to the Information Regulator
The function must be outsourced to an external firm
Oversight must be structured to keep segregation of duties and avoid conflicts
bank.explanation: The standard requires the cyber function to have adequate resources, authority and access to the governing body, structured to ensure segregation of duties and avoid conflicts of interest.

bank.question: A new cyber threat targeting South African banks appears in March. The yearly refresher is in October. What does paragraph 7.2.7 expect?
options: Wait for the October refresher to cover it
Add training on the new content regularly, without waiting for the refresher
Do nothing unless the threat causes an incident
Ask the FSCA to approve new material first
bank.explanation: Besides the yearly refresher, the standard expects training on new content to be done regularly, considering evolving risks.

bank.question: An agent receives a WhatsApp from someone using the CEO's photo, asking for gift vouchers for a client event and saying 'don't tell anyone, it's a surprise'. Which combination of signs best shows social engineering?
options: A known photo, polite wording and a weekday message
An unusual channel, a request for value and a demand for secrecy
A request linked to a client event
A message sent during business hours
bank.explanation: A senior name on an unusual channel, a request for something of value and pressure to keep it secret are classic lure signals. Polite wording or a known photo do not prove identity.

bank.question: Marula Bank lets staff reach the customer CRM over the internet from home. Only a password is required. Which Joint Standard 2 requirement is most clearly at risk?
options: Biennial review of the asset inventory
Yearly review of the cyber strategy
MFA for accounts that access applications with sensitive information through the internet
Notification of material incidents to the authority
bank.explanation: The standard requires MFA for all user accounts used to access applications containing sensitive information through the internet, and strong authentication for remote access.

bank.question: A system administrator also approves her own access requests and reviews the logs of her own privileged account. Which Joint Standard 2 principles are breached?
options: Data minimisation and purpose specification
Segregation of duties and review of privileged account activity
Board approval of the cyber strategy
Penetration testing frequency
bank.explanation: The standard requires segregation of duties when granting access, and privileged account use must be logged and reviewed as part of monitoring. Self-approval and self-review defeat both.

bank.question: Which statement about the SARB's warning on advance-fee scams is accurate?
options: The SARB confirms it holds foreign funds for individuals on request
The SARB says such scams only arrive by post
Scammers have used the SARB's logo and employee names to make lures look real
The SARB tells victims to pay the fees and then complain
bank.explanation: The SARB says syndicates have abused its corporate identity, using its logo and employee names, through letters, email, SMS, WhatsApp and social media. It does not hold funds for the public.

bank.question: A staff member clicked a phishing link and entered her password, then felt embarrassed and waited a day before telling anyone. Why is this delay the biggest problem?
options: The bank can no longer find out who clicked
Joint Standard 2 requires dismissal after any click
It gives the attacker time to use the credentials before they are reset
Reporting is only possible on the same day
bank.explanation: Speed matters most after a compromise. Prompt reporting lets the security team reset credentials, check activity and contain spread. A blame-free reporting culture supports this.

bank.question: Joint Standard 2 requires controls against 'unauthorised internet services'. Which staff behaviour does this target most directly?
options: Using the bank's approved email system
Logging in with MFA
Using personal cloud storage or messaging apps to send or store sensitive data
Completing the yearly awareness refresher
bank.explanation: The standard requires security controls to prevent and detect the use of unauthorised internet services that let users communicate or store sensitive data.

bank.question: A caller to the contact centre says he is from IT support and asks the agent to read out the one-time PIN just sent to her phone 'to fix the login'. What should the agent do?
options: Refuse, end the call and report it, because no genuine helper needs a one-time PIN
Share the PIN because IT support is internal
Share half the PIN to test the caller
Ask the caller for his employee number and then share it
bank.explanation: A one-time PIN is a second factor. Sharing it hands the attacker the account. An employee number can also be faked; verify through trusted channels instead.

bank.question: Which design choice reflects the Joint Standard 2 requirement to reduce exposure from web browsing?
options: Allowing browsing only on administrator accounts
Blocking the bank's own website
Running browsing on the core banking server
Separating internet browsing from sensitive systems physically or logically
bank.explanation: The standard requires internet browsing to be isolated from sensitive IT systems through physical or logical segregation, or equivalent controls.

bank.question: Under Joint Standard 2, who should perform periodic user access reviews to confirm that privileges are still appropriate?
options: Appropriate parties such as the owners of the IT systems and information assets
Each user for their own access
The Information Regulator
The external auditor only, every five years
bank.explanation: The standard requires appropriate parties such as system and information asset owners to perform periodic user access reviews.

bank.question: A loan officer asks applicants for their religion and political affiliation 'to understand them better'. Which POPIA problems arise?
options: It is excessive for the purpose and touches special personal information
None, if the applicant answers voluntarily on a form
Only an information quality problem
Only an openness problem, solved by a privacy notice
bank.explanation: Minimality requires information to be adequate, relevant and not excessive, and religion and political persuasion are special personal information that is prohibited unless an authorisation applies.

bank.question: Marula Bank uses a card processor that handles customer card data. The contract does not mention security. What does section 21 of POPIA require?
options: Nothing, because operators are separately licensed
Only an annual phone call to the processor
A notice to the Regulator naming the processor
A written contract ensuring the operator establishes and maintains section 19 security measures
bank.explanation: Section 21(1) requires the responsible party, by written contract, to ensure the operator establishes and maintains the security measures in section 19.

bank.question: A bank keeps closed-account files for many years because a law requires certain records to be kept. Does POPIA's retention condition stop this?
options: Yes: all records must be deleted on account closure
Yes: unless the customer consents in writing each year
No: retention is allowed when the law requires or authorises it
No: POPIA has no retention rule at all
bank.explanation: Section 14(1) allows records to be kept longer than the purpose needs when retention is required or authorised by law, among other exceptions. After that, they must be destroyed or de-identified.

bank.question: Which statement about personal information under POPIA is correct?
options: It can include information about an identifiable existing juristic person, such as a company
It covers only information about individuals over 18
It excludes ID numbers and account numbers
It covers only information stored on paper
bank.explanation: POPIA defines personal information as relating to an identifiable living natural person and, where applicable, an identifiable existing juristic person.

bank.question: A staff member knowingly obtains a customer's account number without the bank's consent and sells it to a third party. How does POPIA treat this?
options: Only as a disciplinary matter for HR
As an offence, with a possible fine or imprisonment of up to 10 years
As a civil matter with no criminal consequence
As lawful if the buyer is a bank customer
bank.explanation: Section 106 makes knowingly or recklessly obtaining or disclosing an account number without consent, and selling one so obtained, an offence; section 107 sets a fine or imprisonment of up to 10 years.

bank.question: Which factor must the Information Regulator consider when setting an administrative fine under section 109?
options: The bank's share price on the day of the breach
Whether the bank has a branch in Gauteng
The number of data subjects affected or potentially affected
The age of the information officer
bank.explanation: Section 109(3) lists factors including the nature of the information, the duration and extent of the contravention, the number of people affected and the likelihood of substantial damage or distress.

bank.question: A bank processes customer information for FIC Act customer due diligence without asking for consent. Which section 11 ground most clearly supports this?
options: The bank's marketing interest
The customer's implied consent by walking into a branch
Processing complies with an obligation imposed by law on the bank
No ground is needed for regulated banks
bank.explanation: Section 11(1)(c) allows processing that complies with an obligation imposed by law on the responsible party, such as the bank's duties under the FIC Act.

bank.question: Under section 19(3), what must a bank have due regard to when designing security safeguards for personal information?
options: Only the cheapest available technology
Generally accepted information security practices and any industry rules that apply to it
The preferences of the bank's largest customer
Whatever its operators propose
bank.explanation: Section 19(3) requires due regard to generally accepted information security practices and procedures, including those required by specific industry or professional rules. For banks this includes the Joint Standards.

bank.question: Marula's information officer wants to show how POPIA's security condition and Joint Standard 2 fit together. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Both require risk-based safeguards, and the bank must meet each in full
Joint Standard 2 replaces POPIA for banks
POPIA replaces Joint Standard 2 for customer data
Only one applies, chosen by the board each year
bank.explanation: POPIA and Joint Standard 2 are separate obligations enforced by different authorities. Strong controls can satisfy both, but neither replaces the other.

bank.question: Marula Bank detects ransomware at 22:00 on Monday and, after triage, classifies it as material at 10:00 on Tuesday. By when is the immediate notification on Umoja due under the template?
options: By 22:00 on Tuesday, 24 hours after detection
By 10:00 on Wednesday, 24 hours after classification
By the following Monday
Within 14 days of detection
bank.explanation: The template's clock runs from classification as material, not from detection: immediate notification is due within 24 hours following classification. Classification itself should not be delayed without reason.

bank.question: During a material incident, investigators find that attackers copied 3,000 customers' payslips. The police ask in writing for customer notices to wait five days. Which approach is correct?
options: Notify nobody until the police finish
Notify customers immediately, ignoring the police
Notify only the PA, because the police are involved
Notify the PA and the Regulator, record the police request, and notify customers when the delay ends
bank.explanation: The PA notice follows the Joint Notice timelines. Under section 22, the Regulator is still notified, and only the customer notice may be delayed where a public body investigating offences decides notice would impede its investigation.

bank.question: Which document did Joint Notice 2 of 2026 determine as the form for notifying material IT and cyber incidents?
options: The FIC's suspicious transaction report form
The Information Regulator's PAIA manual template
The Reporting of Material IT and Cyber Incident Template (Annexure A)
A free-form letter to the PA's CEO
bank.explanation: The Joint Notice determines the 'Reporting of Material IT and Cyber Incident Template', attached as Annexure A, as the information banks must submit.

bank.question: A contained phishing incident affects five staff mailboxes, with no customer impact and no service disruption. The bank's criteria say it is not material. What follows under Joint Standard 2?
options: The PA must be notified within 24 hours anyway
The incident can be deleted from the records
The Information Regulator must always be notified
No PA notice is needed, but the bank still manages and learns from it under its plan
bank.explanation: Notification under paragraph 9.1 follows classification as material. Non-material incidents are still handled, investigated and used for lessons under the response plan. POPIA s 22 applies only if personal information was reached.

bank.question: Which statement correctly describes the trigger for the PA notice under the Joint Standards?
options: It follows the bank classifying the incident as material
It follows any phishing email received by staff
It follows the incident being reported in the media
It follows the Information Regulator's request
bank.explanation: Both Joint Standard 1 paragraph 15.1 and Joint Standard 2 paragraph 9.1 tie notification to the bank classifying the event or incident as material.

bank.question: The template asks whether 'any other regulatory authority, such as the Information Regulator' has been notified. What does this tell the incident team?
options: Choose one regulator and ignore the other
Let the PA forward the information to the Regulator
Wait for the PA to decide on POPIA
Coordinate the PA notice and any POPIA notice and record both
bank.explanation: The template expects the bank to say which other authorities were told. POPIA notice is the bank's own duty and is not passed on by the PA, so the team must handle both.

bank.question: Joint Standard 2 requires backups of sensitive information to be protected. Which practice meets the standard best?
options: Encrypted backups stored offline or offsite, including suitable cloud storage
Unencrypted backups on the same server as production
Backups kept only on staff laptops
No backups, relying on the vendor's goodwill
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.4.1 requires sensitive information in backup media to be secured, for example encrypted, and backup media to be stored offline or at an offsite location, which can include cloud storage.

bank.question: In the Justice department's 2021 ransomware case, which response did the department report on gov.za?
options: It paid the ransom and restored all systems in one day
It shut down the courts for a month
It reported that no personal information was involved at any stage
It activated its business continuity plan and later notified data subjects on its website
bank.explanation: Its statements said it activated its business continuity plan, kept courts running manually, and after assessing a possible leak issued a POPIA notice to data subjects on its website.

bank.question: A bank's resilience team mapped only its own staff and systems for its critical payments operation, ignoring its card processor and cloud host. Which Directive 4 categories are most clearly weak?
options: Information quality and openness
Mapping interconnections and third-party dependency management
Purpose specification and retention
Capital adequacy and liquidity
bank.explanation: Mapping must cover interconnections and interdependencies of critical operations, and third-party dependency management covers providers they rely on. The other options are POPIA conditions or unrelated risks.

bank.question: A bank group asks whether Directive 4 of 2023 applies only to the licensed bank or across the group. What does the directive say?
options: Only to the licensed bank, never to subsidiaries
Only to foreign subsidiaries
The principles must be applied on a consolidated basis
Only to entities with more than 1,000 staff
bank.explanation: The directive states that the principles must be applied on a consolidated basis and form part of a forward-looking resilience approach in line with risk appetite and tolerance for disruption.

bank.question: The board asks why operational resilience is a matter of capital, not only of IT. Which point from Directive 4 answers best?
options: Resilience costs are deducted from capital automatically
The FSCA sets capital for IT projects
POPIA fines are paid out of regulatory capital
Regulation 38(4) lets the PA require additional capital if resilience policies are inadequate
bank.explanation: Directive 4 explains that where the PA considers a bank's resilience policies inadequate, regulation 38(4) allows it to require extra capital or alignment of policies with risk exposure.

bank.question: Marula Bank's internet banking platform had a major update in March. Its last penetration test was in January. What does Joint Standard 2 require?
options: Nothing until next January
A test only if customers complain
A penetration test to validate controls after the major update
A test only if the PA asks for one
bank.explanation: For systems directly accessible from the internet, penetration testing is required whenever they undergo major changes or updates, and at least yearly where there are no major changes.

bank.question: Testing reveals a critical flaw in a new mobile app the week before launch. Under Joint Standard 2's remediation rules, what should happen?
options: Launch on time and fix it in the next quarter
Launch and disclose the flaw on social media
Fix the known major flaw before the app goes into production
Ask customers to accept the risk in the terms
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.7.6 requires known major issues and security flaws to be remediated before production deployment, with all testing issues tracked.

bank.question: Which piece of evidence best shows the PA that Marula meets the paragraph 7.2.7 training duty?
options: A copy of the cyber policy on the intranet
Completion records for all users, board training records and the latest programme review
A single email reminding staff to be careful
The vendor's brochure for the e-learning tool
bank.explanation: The duty covers all users, yearly refreshers, regular new content, board training and periodic review. Evidence should show each of these, not just that a policy exists.

bank.question: Joint Standard 2 requires banks to take part in cyber threat information sharing. What is the main aim?
options: To share and receive timely, actionable information on threats, vulnerabilities and incidents
To publish customers' personal information
To replace the bank's own monitoring
To advertise the bank's security products
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.6.2 requires participation in information-sharing arrangements with trusted external parties to share reliable, actionable information and receive timely threat information.

bank.question: A data scientist wants to test a new model using a full copy of production customer data in a development environment without production-level controls. What does Joint Standard 2 require?
options: Restrict it unless equivalent controls exist; exceptions need safeguards and senior management approval
Allow it, because development is internal
Allow it if the data scientist signs a POPIA declaration
Allow it only on weekends
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7.2.3 restricts sensitive information in non-production environments unless equivalent controls are in place; in exceptional cases there must be safeguards and senior management approval, with masking where possible.

bank.question: Which combination best summarises what a South African bank must evidence in this quest's area?
options: Only POPIA, because it is an Act
Only Joint Standard 2, because it is the newest
Only the FIC Act, because it covers all bank risk
Directive 4 resilience, Joint Standards 1 and 2 governance and cyber controls, and POPIA privacy safeguards
bank.explanation: Each instrument has its own scope and authority: the PA's directive, the joint PA and FSCA standards, and POPIA enforced by the Information Regulator. The bank must evidence each on its own terms.
